subject: Renewal: Portfolio tier + top-up options and co-terming
messages:
From: Ellen Ross <ellen.ross@averylabs.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@averylabs.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-contract top-up and co-terming options

Hi Jordan,

We're seeing a material uptick in usage for our search & summarization flows and need to top up capacity mid-contract. A few asks from procurement before we move forward:

- Can you outline pricing for a one-time top-up of 200 GPU-hours (monthly equivalent) vs annualizing that capacity into our existing yearly commitment?
- If we annualize, what discount tiers apply and how does co-terming work (we're trying to align everything to 2027-03-31)?
- Any changes to invoice timing / PO requirements for a mid-cycle amendment?

Attached is our Q3 usage extract so you can see the spike. We'd like to get a sense of options by next week to inform our internal budget review.

Thanks — Ellen

Ellen Ross
Director, Platform Engineering
Avery Labs
Attachments: Q3_usage_report.csv
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ellen Ross <ellen.ross@averylabs.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-contract top-up and co-terming options

Hi Ellen — thanks for the data, that makes the spike clear. High-level options below; Ben and Naomi I've looped you in to confirm price bands and procurement logistics. Draft proposal attached.

Option 1 — One-time top-up (short-term)
- 200 GPU-hours purchased as a 3-month prepaid add-on
- No change to existing renewal date; billed on our standard invoice terms
- Effective price: list rate less 5% standard short-term add-on discount

Option 2 — Annualize into commitment (recommended if sustained)
- Convert the equivalent of 200 GPU-hours/month into annual committed units
- Eligibility for uplift discount: 12% on the incremental annualized units if committed for remaining term (pro-rated)
- We can co-term to 2027-03-31 by creating an amendment that annualizes the extra units and re-prices to an annual rate; invoice timing would switch to your normal quarterly/annual schedule per PO

Option 3 — Hybrid (bridge + annualize)
- Immediate 3-month top-up at 0% discount to cover the shortfall, followed by a pending amendment to annualize starting next quarter with a 10% uplift credit applied retroactively to the months after amendment execution

Next steps: Ben — can you confirm the exact pro-rate math and whether legal needs a special clause for invoice timing? Naomi — if the customer wants to co-term to 2027-03-31, what internal steps do we need for approval?

Attached: proposal-draft.pdf

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ellen Ross <ellen.ross@averylabs.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-contract top-up and co-terming options

Jordan / Naomi — quick pricing note (putting numbers to the options):

Assumptions: 200 GPU-hours/month ~= 2,400 GPU-hours/year. Current list price per GPU-hour: $3.50 (example).

Option 1 (3-month prepaid)
- Price per hour: $3.32 (5% off list)
- Total: 200 * 3 * $3.32 = $1,992
- Invoiced immediately; no amendment to MSAs required beyond a PO for the add-on

Option 2 (annualize & co-term)
- If customer annualizes for remainder of term (6.5 months remaining to 2027-03-31), we pro-rate the 2,400h to 1,300h (2,400 * 6.5/12)
- Discount banding: standard uplift discount 12% if customer commits to the incremental annualized units for the remaining term; if they want to extend to a new 12-month add-on we can increase to 15%
- Effective blended price for pro-rated period: $3.08/hr after 12%

Option 3 (hybrid)
- Bridge months billed at list (no discount) to avoid revenue leakage; apply a one-time credit equal to 10% of the bridged months if amendment executes within 60 days

Operational notes:
- Procurement: we can accept a PO for the add-on; amendments that change committed units require countersignature and DocuSign (legal needs to approve amendment language but this is standard).
- Billing lead time: if they want invoice changes (quarterly instead of monthly), we need procurement to confirm PO/terms; finance needs ~5 business days to adjust the cadence.

I've attached the pricing_playbook_v3.xlsx with the math and example line items. Jordan, if Ellen wants a clean single-line amendment that annualizes and co-terms, recommend Option 2 with the 12% band and a 30-day signature SLA.
- Ben
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing_playbook_v3.xlsx
From: Ellen Ross <ellen.ross@averylabs.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@averylabs.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-contract top-up and co-terming options

Thanks Jordan and Ben — appreciate the clarity. Internally we've reviewed and prefer the hybrid path with a fast annualize (Option 3) but with a tweak: can we shorten the co-term adjustment window to 90 days instead of 120/annualized negotiation? Procurement prefers the bridge while legal reviews, then formalize to co-term by Dec 18, 2026. If you can provide a 10% retroactive credit for bridge months (as you outlined) and confirm the amendment will not change existing SLAs, we'll route the PO this week.

Also: can you confirm whether DocuSign will be acceptable for our procurement team (we have a standard signer)? If so, please include the purchaser name formatting for the PO to match our legal entity: "Avery Labs, Inc."

Thanks — Ellen

Ellen Ross
Director, Platform Engineering
Avery Labs
